blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Average represents the central value obtained by dividing the sum of all observations by the total count.
To find the sum of a series, multiply the given average by the number of observations.
Adding or removing a value alters both the total sum and the total count of observations.
Age problems require adjusting the average based on the passage of time for all members in a group.
Weighted average calculates the overall average when different groups have varying sizes or importance.
Average of a group of numbers is a single value that represents the central value of the group.

Formula:

Average = (Sum of observations) / (Number of observations)

blocks.content: In SBIexamination, questions on average are direct, formula-based, and often linked with age, salary, marks, population and similar topics.

blocks.content: 3. FINDING SUM WHEN AVERAGE IS GIVEN

items:
Formula:

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Example:

Average age of 10 students is 18 years.

Total age = 18 × 10 = 180 years

blocks.content: 4. AVERAGE WHEN A VALUE IS ADDED OR REMOVED

Example 1:

Average of 5 numbers is 20. A new number 30 is added.

Old sum = 20 × 5 = 100

New sum = 100 + 30 = 130

New number of observations = 6

New average = 130 / 6 ≈ 21.67



Example 2:

Average of 10 numbers is 25. One number 35 is removed.

Old sum = 25 × 10 = 250

New sum = 250 − 35 = 215

New number of observations = 9

New average = 215 / 9 ≈ 23.89

items: Average age of 5 boys is 20 years and average age of 3 girls is 18 years.
Sum of boys = 5 × 20 = 100
Sum of girls = 3 × 18 = 54
Total sum = 154

blocks.content:
• Always calculate total sum first.

• Be careful when values are added or removed.

• Average depends on sum and number of terms.

• SBIquestions are generally simple and direct.

items: Always account for changes in the total count (n + 1 or n - 1) when an item is added or removed.
In average age problems, remember that time increments equally for every member of the group.
Weighted average questions frequently test combining two groups with different sample sizes.
